description: Shared Zaude Master Prompts for the AI Prompt Advancer. Select one or more options when advancing a prompt to steer camera language, fight choreography, dialogue acting, RefMod continuity, soundscape, or local LTX pacing.

masters.name: Cinema Camera Rules
masters.description: 180° rule, motivated dolly/track moves, explicit lens (35mm/50mm/85mm), foreground depth, zero unmotivated floating camera.
masters.instructions: Apply strict cinematography rules: specify exact shot size and lens focal length (e.g. 35mm wide, 50mm medium, 85mm close-up), respect the 180-degree screen-direction rule, use ONE motivated camera move (slow push-in, steady tracking shot, handheld micro-shake, or locked tripod) rather than random floating motion, establish foreground/midground/background depth layers, and lock lighting direction and color temperature.

masters.name: Better Fights & Action
masters.description: Clear wind-up → impact → follow-through beats, crisp spatial staging, camera impact jolt, weight & debris.
masters.instructions: Choreograph the action as a crisp, readable beat-by-beat physical sequence: (1) telegraph/wind-up, (2) decisive impact with real weight and momentum transfer, (3) immediate physical reaction/stumble/fall, (4) brief hold to read the aftermath. Keep spatial geography crystal clear (explicitly state screen-left vs screen-right staging), add a subtle camera jolt on impact followed by quick stabilization, include environmental contact cues (dust, sparks, footsteps, cloth snap), and avoid rubbery slow-motion or teleporting limbs.

masters.name: Dialogue & Acting
masters.description: Timestamped Dialogue windows, micro-expressions, eye-line lock, natural gestures, RefMod speaking block.
masters.instructions: Structure speaking scenes for strong lip-sync and acting: include explicit timestamped dialogue windows (e.g. Dialogue (0.6s–4.2s): Subject 1 says "..."), specify eye-line direction, subtle facial micro-expressions (brow furrow, breath inhale, glance away), and grounded hand/posture beats. For RefMod shots, include a concise RefMod usage note (visible=...; speaking=...) so the right character speaks.

masters.name: Strict RefMod Lock
masters.description: Default outfit negation, verbatim room/prop anchors, bright TV/screen lock ON, zero identity drift.
masters.instructions: Enforce strict MiniMax-H3 RefMod continuity: refer to characters as Subject 1 (<Name>), Subject 2 (<Name>). Whenever wardrobe differs from a character's default RefMod look, explicitly negate the default first ("NOT in default outfit, instead wearing..."). Repeat concrete room/prop/lighting anchors verbatim, keep any TV/monitor screens explicitly brightly lit and ON, and lock wardrobe and hair state across the full shot.

masters.name: Rich Sound & Foley
masters.description: Detailed overall_soundscape (foley, footsteps, room tone) + non_diegetic_music cues for H3 joint audio-video.
masters.instructions: Add dedicated joint audio-video sections tailored for MiniMax-H3: include an `overall_soundscape:` paragraph detailing concrete foley synced to visual beats (footsteps on specific floor material, impact thuds, cloth rustle, breathing, ambient room tone) and a `non_diegetic_music:` line describing score instrumentation, tension build, and exact hit/cut-out moments (or explicitly state 'None' if pure diegetic realism is desired).

masters.name: Suspense & Atmosphere
masters.description: Slow dread build, chiaroscuro rim light, negative space, lingering holds before the reveal.
masters.instructions: Heighten tension and mood: use deliberate slow pacing, dramatic chiaroscuro lighting with deep shadows and a single motivated key/rim light, purposeful negative space in the frame, subtle environmental dread cues (flickering light, drifting dust/mist, distant creak), and a lingering beat before any sudden reveal or movement.

masters.name: Comedic Timing
masters.description: Setup → beat pause → deadpan reaction or physical gag, readable two-shot framing.
masters.instructions: Optimize for comedic readability: frame wide enough to keep both the trigger and the reaction clearly visible, build a clear three-beat rhythm (confident setup → half-second beat pause → deadpan expression or physical payoff), keep lighting clean and readable, and emphasize expressive eye movement and posture.

masters.name: Local LTX 2B Tuned
masters.description: Compact single-shot visual prose tuned for fast 8-step LTX-Video 2B GGUF on 8 GB laptops.
masters.instructions: Tailor the prompt for fast 8-step LTX-Video 2B GGUF on an 8 GB GPU: write ONE cohesive, vivid paragraph (under 650 characters) describing a single continuous shot with NO scene cuts, ONE clear primary motion arc, concrete subject appearance, simple readable lighting, and smooth camera motion. Avoid complex multi-character dialogue or dense text overlays.

masters.name: Change Background
masters.description: Preserve performer, pose, timing & camera path from <Video 1> while replacing ONLY the world + matching rim light.
masters.instructions: Format for clean RV2V background replacement: explicitly preserve the performer's exact face, hair, clothing, choreography, poses, timing, and camera trajectory from <Video 1>, replace ONLY the background environment with rich concrete scenery, and specify matching rim lighting, color bounce, and grounded floor contact shadows so the performer blends seamlessly into the new location.

masters.name: Character-Swappable Shot
masters.description: Locks lens, camera move, lighting, and timed 0s–5s beats so swapping any RefMod outputs the exact same shot.
masters.instructions: Structure the prompt as a reusable, character-swappable shot template: use `Subject 1 (<Name>)` keeping their exact RefMod appearance, specify ONE fixed focal length and ONE motivated camera move, anchor concrete environment/props/lighting direction + Kelvin color temperature, choreograph explicit timed physical beats (0s–2s, 2s–4s, 4s–6s), and include `overall_soundscape:` and `non_diegetic_music:` so different characters always produce the same consistent shot.

masters.name: Zaude Multi-Shot Script
masters.description: Full Zaude cinematic syntax: Initial Posture→Impact→Final Pose, 180° OTS, 2.0–2.5 wps <d> dialogue, RefMods, BG locks & --- blocks.
masters.instructions: Write in Zaude's full Cinematic Multi-Shot syntax: enforce strict physical action chains (Initial Posture -> Trigger -> Action -> Momentum -> Impact -> Final Pose), obey coordinate rules (screen-left/right, camera-left/right, subject left/right), maintain 33% face close-ups / 67% environmental-prop shots and 180° paired OTS for two-person dialogue, pace dialogue at 2.0–2.5 words/sec (never >3.0, one speaker per window, start 0.2–0.3s in, end ≥0.2s before shot ends, wrap in <d>[English] ...</d>, never add the 0.917s continuation overlap). Include style_definitions:, subject_definitions: (with RefMod slugs and outfit overrides), retention_analysis: + RefMod usage, detailed_description:, [Shot N] with summary: and timed beats, overall_soundscape:, and non_diegetic_music:. Separate multiple shots with ---.
